text:
<edits>
component: harness.py
candidates: inv1, dom1, inv2, dom2, inv3, dom3, agg1, agg2, agg3 (all candidates identical)
change: Added regex-based extraction of ```python...``` code blocks via `re.findall(r'```python\n(.*?)\n```', reply, re.DOTALL)`, execution via `tools.python()`, and fallback to text extraction if no code block found. Base harness returned only the last line of LLM reply without executing any code.
observed: base1/base2/base3 diverged on the same deterministic computation, returning 91, 90, and 98 respectively. The LLM asserted different intermediate values for 91^14 in each run (471292097996578896321, 58,871,586,708,267,913,281, 2,946,944,980,097,921). All nine candidates with code extraction show [python] execution blocks producing consistent result: 91^14 = 2670419511272061205254504361, digit sum = 91. No candidate diverged.
verdict: helped

component: prompts/task.md
candidates: inv1, dom1, inv2, dom2, inv3, dom3, agg1, agg2, agg3 (all candidates identical)
change: Added instruction "Solve this by writing and executing Python code. Show the code and provide the final numeric answer." after the question placeholder. Base prompt was bare question only.
observed: Base rollouts show no ```python...``` code blocks in LLM responses—LLM attempted mental arithmetic and asserted different results. All candidate rollouts show LLM generating ```python...``` code blocks in response to the explicit code generation request, which the harness then extracted and executed. Library evidence (holdout-numeric-005 decisions) shows extraction without instruction still resulted in fallback to manual reasoning (inv2/inv3/agg1 in that task), while extraction paired with instruction triggered code generation and deterministic execution (dom3/agg2/agg3 in that task).
verdict: confounded

component: prompts/system.md
candidates: none (unchanged)
change: No change; retained "You are a helpful assistant."
observed: No trajectory divergence attributable to system prompt; all candidates behavior consistent with base on this dimension.
verdict: no observed effect
</edits>

<experience>
cue: A numerical computation task where unaided LLM reasoning diverges across runs on the same deterministic problem (e.g., arithmetic, exponentiation, digit sum), with different final answers traced to hallucinated intermediate values in text assertion.

lesson: In harness.py, extract and execute ```python\n(.*?)\n``` code blocks from the LLM reply via regex and tools.python(), returning the last line of execution output and falling back to text extraction only if no code block is present. Pair this mechanism with an explicit task prompt instruction requesting Python code generation ("Solve this by writing and executing Python code. Show the code and provide the final numeric answer."), ensuring the LLM generates executable code blocks and the harness executes them deterministically instead of trusting text assertions.

evidence: All nine candidates applied both edits to harness.py and task.md identically. All nine achieved deterministic answer 91 in [python] execution blocks, eliminating divergence. The harness.py extraction+execution edit directly caused code to be executed rather than asserted (helped). The task.md instruction edit directly caused code blocks to appear in LLM responses, where they would not appear in base (necessary for extraction to be useful). Library precedent holdout-numeric-002 and holdout-numeric-005 document identical pattern (base divergence from assertion, all candidates with both components converged on correct answer) with medium-to-high confidence. Library holdout-numeric-005 further establishes that extraction without instruction still diverged (inv2/inv3/agg1 fell back to manual reasoning), confirming both components are necessary as a pair for deterministic execution of numeric computation.

confidence: medium. The extraction mechanism clearly helped (base diverged, all candidates with extraction converged). The instruction directly triggered code generation observable in trajectories (library evidence confirms instruction + extraction are a necessary pair). However, this task cannot isolate the individual contribution of each component since all nine candidates apply both together. The transfer confidence rests entirely on library precedent showing the paired pattern solves the same problem class in two prior tasks, which is substantial but not a direct replication.
</experience>
